findings.review_scope: Registered-source content review of arXiv:2112.10151v2, stamped 2 April 2024, by Jinyuan Chang, Qiao Hu, Eric D. Kolaczyk, Qiwei Yao and Fengting Yi. The PDF has 76 pages. Main text ends immediately above the APPENDIX heading on shared page 19 at y=313.6376953125. Fresh text covers pages 1-18 and only the main-text portion of page 19. The boundary heading was inspected in a separate heading-only crop; no appendix or embedded supplement body was read.
findings.inventory: Exactly four actual THEOREM headings occur, at pages 9,12,13,18. Theorem 1 continues on page 10. All hypotheses, conclusions, formulas and subparts match the rendered source. Proposition, Remark and theorem citations do not enter this inventory.
original_statements: Theorem 1 preserves Condition 1, the printed extra script-I membership chain, fixed s and distinct coordinates, all three privacy regimes, and the different normalizations involving b, tilde-b and their combination. The full third case on page 10 remains included.

Theorem 2 retains its reference to the conditions of Theorem 1, delta in (0,c] with c<0.5, its own gamma window, fixed s and both parts. The bootstrap estimate is centered at the original population parameter theta, not theta-hat. Its population variance ratio has deterministic O(delta) error.

Theorem 3 retains the stronger gamma window and smaller delta bound, the supremum over all p-dimensional lower orthants, the original estimator theta-hat and the diagonal population bootstrap variance V-dagger. It does not use Monte Carlo variance estimates or state conditional bootstrap convergence.

Theorem 4 retains the sparse parametrization, narrowed omega restrictions, all three tilde-O_p terms and the deterministic fourth term, their exact powers, the printed equality chain and its complete gamma lower bound. The unparenthesized minus/max formula defining chi_p remains as printed.
source_passages: All 19 local passages and 10 auxiliary passages were reviewed. The beta-model product likelihood gives independent undirected Bernoulli edges on fixed labeled simple networks. Jittering retains both asymmetric flip probabilities, three-point noise and the strict interior class M. Condition 1 remains a separate dense-model parameter bound.

The original correction functions, population triangle moments, unordered averaging set, empirical triangle products and logarithmic estimator match pages 7-8. Lambda, b and tilde-b match page 9, including the ordered double sum and factor 1/(2N). N=(p-1)(p-2) and the combined nu are preserved. The source does not specify a fallback for a nonpositive empirical ratio.

The second symmetric jittering stage, bootstrap correction, bootstrap estimator and population analogues match pages 11-12. The expectation identities resolve the variance law as the population law over both noise stages. The later sample variance over repeated bootstrap draws is distinct and is not imported into Theorems 2/3.

The sparse beta-model, nonnegative effects, zero minimum, support size s=o(p), logarithmic residual parameters and relation theta=xi/2+check-theta match page 17. The unthresholded sparse estimates and paper-specific tilde-O_p convention match page 18. The latter allows some sufficiently small fixed polynomial factor; it is not simply a polylogarithmic convention.
findings.dependency_review: All 20 direct local uses (19 after grouping), all 19 local reach sets, every dependency path and all 33 deduplicated canonical theorem connections were checked. The 12 keyword groups preserve distinct component identities. In particular the original estimator D8 reaches Theorems 1/3/4, while its group also reaches Theorem 2 through population moments D7. The bootstrap estimator D14 reaches only Theorem 2, while its group reaches Theorem 3 through the correction function D13. Original variance nu D11 reaches only Theorem 2; its group also reaches Theorem 1 through D10. Condition 1 reaches only Theorems 1-3. Sparse passages and the stochastic-order convention reach only Theorem 4. No proof-only propositions, adaptive tuning algorithm or empirical bootstrap variance is imported.
findings.names_and_highlights: Each group uses source natural-language keywords. Every member preserves its source heading/type and has selectors in its original passage or related same-paper theorem. The adjacent naming passage for asymptotic variances is on page 10. Grouped component passages are explicitly distinct, not claimed equivalent. Symbol correspondence was inspected in addition to string occurrence.
findings.source_limitations: The 18 existing source notes were checked. They retain the extra script-I membership, chi_p grouping ambiguity, equality of different errors, nonstandard stochastic-order quantifier, logarithm-domain omission, implicit freshness of release noise, nominally overwide gamma range, alternative phase scope, population bootstrap centering, nonnegative/empty-support conventions, erroneous sparse norm display, sparse versus dense assumptions, absence of thresholding, different meanings of s, finite normalization domains, comma versus semicolon in M, denominator-positive privacy convention and excluded appendix references. These observations do not certify the mathematical correctness of the source.
findings.changes: No census-content correction was required. The per-paper rebuild now resolves the verified fixed local PDF and preserves the shared-page clipping boundary. The earlier scripts are archived; the original audit and all six extracted JSON artifacts remain unchanged.
findings.validation: The independent inventory and census validators pass, and all six regenerated artifacts match saved bytes. Source identity, theorem heading enumeration, continuation pages, local and grouped graph checks, selector occurrence and artifact hashes supplement the manual source review.
